payload.evidence:
Tail-orphan trap verified before any console is built on it (ic, HEAD 863cb2f23, re-driven 2026-09-10 10:06:32Z). `int macos app-test`: 21 tests, 0 failures, `Test Suite 'TailOrphanTests' passed` (3 tests, 241.774s), harness terminal line `IntentTests passed`. THE VERDICT IS THE TERMINAL LINE, NOT A PIPELINE rc, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: `cmd_app_test` captures xcodebuild's rc and calls `die` before ever reaching that printf, so the line is emitted ONLY on the rc==0 branch. A rc read off the end of a pipe would have been tail's, not the harness's -- the trap that already produced one false green in this thread, where a wrapper announced `exited with code 0` over an xcodebuild that exited 65. INSTRUMENT: IntentTests/TailOrphanTests.swift driving IntentTests/tail-orphan-probe.sh under /bin/bash 3.2.57 -- NOT PATH bash 5.3.15; the first version used BASHPID (bash 4.0+) and died under xcodebuild while passing for its author, so the interpreter is pinned in the test. THREE SIGNALS SEPARATELY, SIX CELLS: guarded arm clean 3/3 under TERM, INT and KILL; CONTROL arm (plain) LEAKED 3/3. The control is what makes the pass mean anything -- "no tail is running" is also the answer from a probe that never started one, from one that lost its pid, and from one whose fixture failed to launch. RIG SELF-TEST: the third verdict (probe-indeterminate) is proven reachable via the stubborn arm under TERM, with the same arm under KILL as negative control returning LEAKED, because a verdict that cannot be produced is decoration -- it was unreachable when first written and only trying to fire it found that out. 0281's PRECONDITION is asserted inside the probe before any verdict is available: runtime pgid == runtime pid, else probe-refuse at rc=2, because a test that only checks the tail is gone PASSES ON A BUILD THAT KILLED THE APP. CONSTRUCTION UNDER TEST IS THE RULED ONE (0281 option (i)): the wrapper reads its own stdin from a FIFO, the runtime holds the sole write end (3>&- so the wrapper does not hold it, exec so no descendant inherits fd 3), and the group goes down via kill -TERM 0 on EOF however the runtime dies.

SCOPE, STATED BECAUSE A SATISFIED ROW SHOWS ONLY "satisfied" IN THE GATE. This verifies the TRAP and the RULED REMEDY ahead of any console, which is exactly what the row asks for. It does NOT verify product code: IntentCLI.stream has ZERO callers (grep positive-controlled against a known symbol) and the remedy is deliberately not built into the app, because there is no verb to put it in. The doc comment at IntentCLI.swift:158 carries the ruling in the FUTURE tense -- "when a log verb is built, IT runs its pipeline under a shell that reads its own stdin" -- and records that nothing calls it today. THE SUCCESSOR ROW DOES NOT EXIST YET: nothing asserts that the eventual log verb uses this construction, and that gap is named here rather than left for the console's author to discover.

THE ROW'S OWN NAMED METHOD WAS NOT USED, AND USING IT WOULD HAVE BEEN WORTHLESS. "Driving the app open and shut several times and then reading ps" returns zero orphans on a COMPLETELY UNFIXED build, because nothing in the app spawns a tail at all -- so that instrument cannot exhibit the failure it exists to detect and would have passed either way. A stronger instrument was substituted deliberately, and it is recorded here rather than done silently.
